title: Cursor: computer use
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: Three acts with no wasted shot: the claim types on white, the prompt types in a close-up composer, then the agent window and an iOS Simulator sit side by side on an orange gradient while the agent drives the app. 21 s.
instrument: Camera moves are small; one pull ×0.81 at 8.5 s widens to both windows. Most cuts are dissolves.

byEye.zoom: the composer at ×2.5; both windows together at ×1 on the gradient; the phone alone at the end
byEye.cards: 'Cursor can now control your laptop' → 'Use it to drive apps like the iOS simulator' (typed, 7.4 s together); logo
byEye.cursor: the agent's own pointer inside the Simulator
byEye.frame: two windows (dark agent chat, iPhone Simulator) on an orange-to-white gradient

classify: Hand-edited feature reel of real UI, with a typed claim and a two-window composition. Conventions: typed claim, composer close-up, side-by-side windows on a gradient, logo on white.

diagnose.observation: The agent and the app it drives share one frame.
diagnose.principle: Cause and effect in one frame (parallel action without a cut).

diagnose.observation: The last UI shot is the result alone: the Favorites screen.
diagnose.principle: End on the result, isolated from the process that made it.

teaches.text: Two windows side by side on the backdrop: one acting, one acted on.

critique.like: It films an agent the only honest way: you see what it does to a real app.
critique.wish: The agent's log on the left is too small to read; it's texture, not information.
critique.wonder: cutscene could record two pages in one scene and frame them side by side the way this frames agent and Simulator.
